content.text:
Act as the implementation sub-agent for this task.

Repo: inkling (Electron + React + TS, Bun, Windows-only desktop app). Read AGENTS.md at the repo root and follow it. Do the work yourself; no subagents. This machine is Windows, which is the same OS CI will use, so reproduce locally instead of burning CI runs.

## Goal
The `frontend` job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs on `ubuntu-24.04`, so `bun test` (including asset path containment in `electron/storage/shared.ts` `isInside`, which depends on `node:path` separators) only proves POSIX behavior while the app ships on Windows. Move the `frontend` job to `windows-latest` so the full suite runs on the real target OS. (t3code has a Windows test lane in `.github/workflows/windows-tests.yml`; ours runs by default instead of on manual dispatch because our app is Windows-only.)

## Requirements
- Keep the `changes` (path filter) job on ubuntu. Move only `frontend` to `windows-latest`. Keep the job name `Frontend checks` and job id `frontend` unchanged (branch protection may require that name). Do not touch the Linux Xvfb smoke job in `electron-preview.yml` or release workflows.
- Windows runner shell gotcha: the default shell is pwsh, and in a multi-line `run: |` block a failing native command in the middle does NOT fail the step; only the last command's exit code counts. Steps with several commands (the typecheck workspaces step, the canary step) must either use `shell: bash` (GitHub's bash step uses `set -e` semantics) or be split into one command per step. Pick the smallest approach and apply it to every multi-command step.
- Line endings: Windows runners may check out with CRLF, which can make `oxfmt --check` or tests fail. Check `.gitattributes` and the checkout config; make the checkout produce LF the way the repo expects (e.g. a `.gitattributes` eol rule or `git config --global core.autocrlf false` before checkout) if needed. Keep this minimal and only if the evidence shows it is needed.
- Fix any test that fails on Windows. Locally run the full CI frontend sequence once on this machine (this task explicitly authorizes a full `bun test`, `bun run typecheck`, `bun run knip`, `bun run lint`, `bun run build`, `bun run build:app`, `bun run ingest:smoke`; skip steps that are clearly the same on every OS if slow, but do run `bun test`). Also run the typecheck/canary commands as CI does. Fix real failures with the smallest change; if a failure is a genuine Windows-only product bug rather than a test assumption, report it instead of papering over it.
- Update docs that describe CI: `docs/operations/development.md` (CI behavior section) and CONTRIBUTING.md if they say CI runs on Linux. Rewrite the affected sentence; do not append.
- `ci.yml` is not covered by CI's paths-ignore, so CI will run on your PR with the real result. That run is your final proof.

## Delivery (full-send, but YOU do not merge or watch; the parent agent will)
- Branch from latest origin/main (`git fetch origin; git switch -c ci/frontend-on-windows origin/main`). Note #194 recently changed ci.yml, so start from fresh main.
- Conventional commit, e.g. `ci(github): run the frontend checks on windows-latest`. End with your own `Co-Authored-By: <your model name> <noreply@anthropic.com>`.
- Push and open a PR with `gh` (use the `file-pr` skill if you have it). Body: problem in a sentence or two, what changed, one line on proof (local Windows run results + note CI result), end with your model name and harness `(T3 Code)`, then `🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)`.
- Do not merge, enable auto-merge, or call watch_pull_request. No sleeping or polling; look at check state once after pushing and report it.
- Last line of your final message exactly: `PR <full URL>, head <SHA>, checks and reviews <state>`. Above it, 3-8 lines: what you changed, what failed on Windows and how you fixed it, local run timings if useful, doubts.

Switched to a new branch 'ci/frontend-on-windows'
branch 'ci/frontend-on-windows' set up to track 'origin/main'.
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
    paths-ignore:
      # Docs carry no executable code — skip CI entirely
      # when a push only touches these (mixed code+docs pushes still run).
      # Automation config (.entire/) is deliberately NOT ignored: runner
      # prompts execute in automation, so those changes must run checks.
      - "**/*.md"
      - "docs/**"
      - "AGENTS.md"
  pull_request:
    paths-ignore:
      - "**/*.md"
      - "docs/**"
      - "AGENTS.md"

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  changes:
    name: Detect changes
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read
    outputs:
      frontend: ${{ steps.filter.outputs.frontend }}
    steps:
      - name: Check out repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}
          # Full history so the path filter diffs the real change set.
          # A shallow checkout can yield an empty diff and silently skip jobs.
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Filter changed paths
        id: filter
        # Pinned to the v4 tag commit: this job gates security checks, so a
        # hijacked floating tag must not be able to falsify filter outputs.
        uses: dorny/paths-filter@ceb8a2b8f2d89434be7ff52d3de7ec3738c5cc9d # v4.0.3
        with:
          # For PR synchronize events, compare only the newest push with the
          # previous head. The default PR diff compares the whole PR to main,
          # which makes a docs-only follow-up rerun code checks.
          token: ''
          base: ${{ github.event.before || github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          predicate-quantifier: some-with-excludes
          filters: |
            frontend:
              - 'src/**'
              - 'public/**'
              - '!src/seedPersonal.ts'
              - '!public/seed-demo/**'
              - 'benchmarks/**'
              - 'electron/**'
              - 'scripts/**'
              - '.vscode/**'
              - '*.json'
              - '*.jsonc'
              - 't3.json'
              # Workspaces the root tsconfig does not cover.
              - 'extension/**'
              - 'packages/**'
              - '!packages/**/node_modules/**'
              - 'index.html'
              - 'package.json'
              - 'bun.lock'
              - '.bun-version'
              - 'vite.config.ts'
              - 'knip.json'
              - '.oxlintrc.json'
              - '.oxfmtrc.json'
              - 'oxlint-plugin-inkling/**'
              - 'tsconfig.json'
              - 'tsconfig.node.json'
              - '.github/workflows/ci.yml'

  frontend:
    name: Frontend checks
    needs: changes
    if: needs.changes.outputs.frontend == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04

    steps:
      - name: Check out repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Set up Bun
        uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@v2
        with:
          bun-version-file: .bun-version

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: bun install --frozen-lockfile

      # Root tsconfig only includes src, so the extension and shared packages
      # are invisible to `bun run typecheck`. Check each workspace explicitly.
      - name: Typecheck workspaces
        run: |
          bun run typecheck
          bun run --cwd extension typecheck
          bun run --cwd packages/ingestion-shared typecheck
          bun run --cwd packages/contracts typecheck

      - name: 'Canary: real tsc typecheck (non-blocking)'
        if: always()
        continue-on-error: true
        run: |
          bun run typecheck:tsc
          bun run --cwd extension typecheck:tsc
          bun run --cwd packages/ingestion-shared typecheck:tsc
          bun run --cwd packages/contracts typecheck:tsc

      - name: Check documented commands exist
        run: bun run check:refs

      - name: Run unit tests
        run: bun test

      - name: Check for unused code
        run: bun run knip

      - name: Lint and format frontend
        run: bun run lint

      - name: Build frontend
        run: bun run build

      # Runs the app-mode build, whose guard fails if the committed demo seed
      # has leaked back into a shipped bundle. Without this the exclusion is
      # only checked at release time.
      - name: Build frontend for the app
        run: bun run build:app

      - name: Run ingestion smoke tests
        run: bun run ingest:smoke

      # Building the Chrome MV3 extension here catches manifest and bundler
      # regressions long before someone tries to load the unpacked directory.
      - name: Build browser extension
        run: bun run --cwd extension build

result.output:
For early signal, run `bun run check`. `noUnusedLocals` / `noUnusedParameters` are on — the compiler catches dead locals; Knip catches dead exports and dependencies.

## Git hooks

None — there are no local hooks by policy. Formatting, linting, and all other gates run in CI.

## CI behavior (what runs where)

- `ci.yml`: docs-only pushes skip; otherwise the frontend job verifies the Bun version pin, typechecks every workspace, runs tests, `knip`, builds the app and extension, and runs ingestion smoke tests.
- `security.yml`: JavaScript/TypeScript CodeQL on open/reopen and roughly every 4th push, dependency review on every PR; path gating applies to push-to-main only.
- `knip.yml`: scheduled `knip --fix` (every other day) opens a cleanup PR. It strips unused `export` keywords and prunes dependencies; it never deletes files.
- `links.yml`: weekly markdown link check, opens an issue on failures. New custom schemes (`inkling://`) or local hosts go in `.lycheeignore`.
- `electron-preview.yml`: when a same-repository PR has the `preview:win` label, builds and uploads the Windows Electron installer. Electron changes also build the Linux directory package and launch it under Xvfb; pinned model files are cached only in GitHub Actions.
- Automation config (`.entire/`) never skips checks.

## Troubleshooting

- `Expected Bun X, found Y`: install the Bun in `.bun-version`; don't edit the check to match your install.
- `knip --fix` PR is noisy: tune `knip.json` entry/project patterns instead of disabling the workflow.

content.text:
The `frontend` job now runs on `windows-latest`, and the local Windows run of the CI sequence passes. Actions hadn't reported any checks on the PR yet when I looked once, so the CI result is still the open proof.

- **Workflow:** job id `frontend` and name `Frontend checks` are unchanged. `changes`, `electron-preview.yml` and the release workflows are untouched. I set `defaults.run.shell: bash` on the job, which covers the typecheck and canary steps without splitting them. I also reworded the CI sentence in `docs/operations/development.md`. `CONTRIBUTING.md` doesn't mention Linux CI, so I left it alone.
- **Line endings:** no change needed. `.gitattributes` already forces LF on source files, and `oxfmt --check` passes on a default Windows checkout, which has autocrlf on.
- **Failure 1:** one test assumed POSIX separators, `data directory keeps portable precedence...` in `electron/storage.test.ts`. I changed its expectations to use `join` and `resolve`.
- **Failure 2:** four tests passed alone but hit bun's 5s default timeout in the full run: two Tesseract OCR tests, the PDF/system-font spawn probe, and the mascot face-margin test.
  - Bun 1.4.4 ignores a timeout set in `bunfig.toml`. A preload `setDefaultTimeout` only applied to the first test file.
  - I changed the `test` script to `bun test --timeout 30000`, and CI and `check` now run `bun run test`.
  - `AGENTS.md` discourages per-test timeouts, so you may prefer a different fix. If CI runners are slower than this machine, 30s might still not be enough.
- **Local results:**
  - `bun run test`: 292 pass in about 55s.
  - Passing: typecheck on all four workspaces, `check:refs`, `knip`, `lint`, `build`, `build:app`, `ingest:smoke`, and the extension build.
  - The non-blocking canary `typecheck:tsc` still fails on `GPUTexture*` types in `LiquidGlass.tsx`, which isn't OS-specific.
  - `bun install` took about 4 minutes here.
